memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He placed the breastpiece on him and put the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece." - Lev 8:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The breastpiece held twelve precious stones, one for each tribe of Israel. When Aaron entered God's presence, he carried the names of all twelve over his heart.

Nobody was left outside. Not the small tribe, not the troublesome tribe, not the tribe in disgrace. All twelve names went in together, close to the high priest's chest.

That is what intercession looks like. Carrying people into God's presence, not because they are impressive, but because they are yours.

And within that breastpiece were the Urim and Thummim. Scripture never explains exactly what they were or how they worked; they were used to seek God's guidance for the nation. Their mystery is itself instructive — Israel could ask, but God gave the answer on His terms.

We have something better now. Aaron carried Israel's names on stones. Jesus carries His people in a way no ornament could picture: he always lives to intercede for them (Heb 7:25). And He said of His own, No one will snatch them out of my hand (Jn 10:28).

If you are in Christ, your name is over the heart of your High Priest right now, while you read this.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Whose names am I carrying into God's presence in prayer?
2. Does it change anything to know Christ is interceding for me at this moment?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You carry my name before the Father. Teach me to carry others faithfully in prayer as You carry me. Amen.
